PolynomialCovers.jl

PolynomialCovers.jl provides numerical algorithms for computing fibers of polynomial maps

\[P(x) = y\]

using robust geometric constructions.

These methods are particularly useful when studying the global structure of polynomial maps and their monodromy.

Installation

using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/luisjavierhernandez/PolynomialCovers.jl")

Basic Example

The following example computes the roots of a polynomial equation using the cyclic lifting solver.


using PolynomialCovers

# Define polynomial P(x) = x^5 - x + 1
P = PolynomialCover([1, 0, 0, 0, -1, 1])

# Target value
y = 5

# Compute roots of P(x) = y
roots = cyclic_lift_solver(P, y)

println(roots)

Package Structure

The package is organized into several components: • Geometry Geometric primitives in the complex plane such as disks, vertices, and polygonal paths. • Polynomial Covers Representation of polynomial maps and their critical geometry. • Lifting Algorithms Numerical routines for lifting paths through polynomial maps. • Solvers Algorithms for computing fibers of polynomial equations.

Mathematical Background

The algorithms implemented in PolynomialCovers.jl are based on the idea that the solutions of

\[P(x) = y\]

can be computed by lifting paths in the complex plane through the polynomial map

P : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}.

In particular, the package implements numerical algorithms inspired by monodromy methods and path continuation techniques.

Examples


using PolynomialCovers

P = PolynomialCover([1.0, 0.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0])   # z^4 - z^2 + 1

F = fiber(P)

transport_to!(F, 5)

println(F.xs)



# P(z) = z² - 1
P = PolynomialCover([1.0, 0.0, -1.0])

y = 3.0

roots = cyclic_lift_solver(P, y)

println("Solutions of P(x) = $y")
println(roots)

To compare


using PolynomialCovers
using Polynomials

P = PolynomialCover([1.0, 0.0, -1.0, 0.0])   # z³ - z

y = 2.0

roots_lift = cyclic_lift_solver(P, y)

# Compare with classical polynomial root solver
poly = Polynomial([ -y, 0, -1, 1 ])  # z³ - z - y
roots_classical = roots(poly)

println("Cyclic lift solver:")
println(roots_lift)

println("\nClassical roots:")
println(roots_classical)

Reference

The package accompanies the article

Root Finding via Polynomial Monodromy at Infinity: Algorithms and Numerical Perspectives. –-
